blocks.text:
Leaving the big city behind, you will stay at an ecolodge in the jungle. Enjoy a walk through the forest, visit a caboclo home to learn how manioc flour is made, explore the village of Acajatuba and look for animals along the riverbanks after dark.

For an additional charge, you can visit the Meeting of the Waters, where the Rio Negro and Solimões rivers meet. Their waters flow side by side for a considerable distance without fully mixing because of differences in temperature and density.

blocks.text: Salvador reveals Brazil’s African heritage through music, capoeira, cuisine and religious traditions. In the historic centre, you will see Pelourinho, the Lacerda Elevator and the Church of São Francisco. The following day is dedicated to relaxing on the beaches of Praia do Forte.
